limits: The HTTP entry is api.main.app driven by Starlette TestClient with the State DB and workspace dependency-overridden and api.authz.gate_enabled monkeypatched True; the real middlewares (write_gate, security headers, read cache) run, but no live uvicorn socket and no Cloudflare Access JWT path was exercised - cf_access.email_from_request_headers is stubbed to None, so 'anonymous' means no credential at all (the strongest pole) and the signed-in non-writer pole was not measured.

The read requires project_id as well as receipt_id, so a holder of the receipt id alone (without the project id) cannot dereference it. That is deliberate project scoping and was disclosed in the request shape, but it is a strictly narrower reading of 'a caller holding only receipt_id' than 'the receipt id suffices'.

The two privacy call sites are redundant: removing either alone keeps the shipped suite green (M2a/M2b). The composite removal leaks (M2), so the property is guarded, but no shipped test pins either layer individually. For this action the row-level authorizer is not a backstop either - state_acceptances and state_evidence are PUBLIC_STATE_TABLES (core/state_privacy.py:92-100), so an armed untrusted connection may read their rows for unopened projects; those two predicate calls are the whole barrier.

Oracle claims were measured by status code and body only (identical 403 for unopened vs nonexistent project; identical 404 for foreign vs nonexistent receipt). No timing side channel was measured: the scoped lookup and the missing-row lookup are both primary-key SELECTs, but I did not benchmark them.

M5 shows the docstring's 'not whatever was recorded against the attempt afterwards' is unguarded by the shipped suite (green); only my throwaway probe caught it. The criterion as written does not require that stronger property.

Not exercised: the MCP transport (state_graph_read requires writer auth for the whole tool, so get_receipt is not anonymously reachable there; also the tool's description enumerates actions and does not name get_receipt - a discovery gap, not a leak), legacy/foreign data shapes (a receipt with NULL or non-JSON evidence_ids would raise outside the 404 path; no such row was constructed), the full tests/ tree and the web/ Vitest suite, and the running deployment on 127.0.0.1:4444 (that container serves different code, so measuring there is not evidence about 350c8777c7951b2dc45dbffe44388a31e6a59c7a).
